title: Voice sounds
keyIdea: Your voice can make lots of sounds. Some are long: you can stretch sss like a snake until your breath runs out. Some are short: t stops at once, and saying t-t-t is just saying it again. Your voice can be loud or quiet, and high or low, and these are two different things. A tiny mouse squeaks high even when it is loud; a big bear growls low even when it is quiet.
familyTip: Play copy cat in the bath or the car: you make a voice sound (a long sss, a short p, a quiet high squeak, a loud low growl) and your child copies it. Then swap. Ask "Was that long or short?" and "Was it high or low?" Keep loud and high apart: try a quiet high squeak and a loud low boom.

visual.caption: Say each sound. Can you stretch it? Drag each card, or tap it and then tap a box.

lab.caption: Flagship lab: stretch long and short sounds, copy things, fit a voice to a place, use a high-low ladder and build sound patterns.

kid: Say sss like a snake. Keep it going. It is a long sound. You can make it last till your breath runs out.
Now say t. It stops at once. It is a short sound. If you say t-t-t, you just say it lots of times.
Your voice can be loud or soft. Use a soft voice when a baby is asleep. Use a big voice to call a friend far off.
Your voice can go up high, like a mouse: eek! It can go down low, like a bear: grrr. High is not the same as loud.
adult: Ages 3 to 4. Voice sounds is Aspect 3 of Phase One in Letters and Sounds: children explore and tell apart the sounds their own voice can make, through copy-cat games, animal noises and sound stories. Development Matters (2021) asks 3 and 4 year olds to develop phonological awareness, and to use a wider range of vocabulary. Good control of the voice and careful listening get children ready to hear and say the separate sounds in words.

Long and short sounds have a basis in phonetics. Continuant sounds such as s, f, z, sh, m and n can be held for as long as the breath lasts. Stop (plosive) sounds such as t, p, k, b, d and g close the mouth and release at once, so they cannot be stretched, only repeated. Many phonics programmes call these stretchy and bouncy sounds. The z in a buzz is voiced: the voice box hums, which a hand on the throat can feel. The s in a hiss is voiceless.

Common mistakes: calling t-t-t-t a long sound because it went on for a while (it is a short sound repeated); mixing up loud with high and quiet with low, when volume and pitch are separate; and adding uh to stop sounds (tuh, puh), which makes them harder to blend later. Be careful to say t and p as short and crisp as you can.

In the lab your child drags a handle to stretch each sound, then sorts it as long or short. They give a voice sound to a snake, a bee, a clock or a car, slide a voice from whisper to calling voice to suit a place, and drag a dot up or down a ladder for a squeak or a growl, loud or quiet. Last, they build heard patterns from long bars and short dots.

practice.prompt: Which sound can you stretch for a long time?
practice.hint: Try to keep each sound going. Which one lasts?
practice.explain: sss keeps going until your breath runs out. t and p stop at once, so they are short sounds.

practice.prompt: You say t {n} times: t-t-t. How many short sounds did you make?
practice.hint: Each t stops at once. Count each one.
practice.explain: You made {n} short sounds. Saying t again and again is lots of short sounds, not one long one.

practice.prompt: A bee buzzes. Which voice sound copies it?
practice.hint: Put a hand on your throat. Which one hums?
practice.explain: zzz buzzes and hums like a bee. sss is a hiss with no hum, like a snake.

practice.prompt: You hold mmm for {n} claps. Then you hold it for 1 more clap. How many claps long is it now?
practice.hint: mmm can keep going. Count the claps, then 1 more.
practice.explain: {n} claps and 1 more is {=n+1} claps. mmm is long, so it can keep going as you count.

practice.prompt: A big bear growls very quietly. Is the growl high or low?
choices: It is not high or low
practice.hint: Being quiet does not make a sound go up.
practice.explain: The growl is still low. Quiet and loud are not the same as high and low.

pool.prompt: A baby is asleep. Which voice should you use?
pool.hint: Which voice will not wake the baby?
pool.explain: A whisper is quiet, so the baby can keep on sleeping.

pool.prompt: A tiny mouse squeaks very loudly. Is the squeak high or low?
choices: It is not high or low
pool.hint: Being loud does not make a squeak go down.
pool.explain: A mouse squeak is high, loud or quiet. Loud is not the same as low.

pool.prompt: Someone says p-p-p-p. Is p a long sound?
choices: No, p is short. It was said again and again
Yes, it went on a long time
pool.hint: Can you stretch one p? Try it.
pool.explain: p stops at once. p-p-p-p is a short sound said four times.

pool.prompt: Which voice sound goes with a clock?
pool.hint: A clock makes short sounds, again and again.
pool.explain: tick, tock are short sounds, like a clock. sss is a snake and brrrm is a car.

pool.prompt: A grown-up says {n} long sounds and 1 short sound. How many sounds is that?
pool.hint: Count the long ones, then add the short one.
pool.explain: {n} long sounds and 1 short sound make {=n+1} sounds.

pool.prompt: A friend is far away in the park. Which voice helps them hear you?
pool.hint: Far away needs a voice that carries.
pool.explain: A big calling voice carries far. A whisper is for someone very close.

pool.prompt: Which of these is a short sound?
pool.hint: Which one stops as soon as you say it?
pool.explain: t stops at once, so it is short. mmm and fff can stretch.

pool.prompt: A pattern has {n} short dots and {k} long bars. How many sounds is that?
pool.hint: Count the dots, then the bars, all together.
pool.explain: {n} dots and {k} bars make {=n+k} sounds in the pattern.

pool.prompt: A snake hisses. Which voice sound copies it?
pool.hint: A hiss has no hum. Feel your throat.
pool.explain: sss hisses like a snake. zzz hums like a bee.

pool.prompt: A grown-up says: sss t sss. Which pattern is it?
pool.hint: Can you stretch each one? sss, then t, then sss.
pool.explain: sss is long, t is short, sss is long: long, short, long.
